title: What If Woodpeckers Grounded a Space Shuttle? In 1995 They Did

scenes.text: What if woodpeckers grounded a space shuttle? In 1995 they did, and NASA fought back with plastic owls.
June 1995. The shuttle Discovery stood on its Florida launch pad, days from lift-off, its giant orange fuel tank coated in soft foam.
To a northern flicker, a woodpecker in nesting season, that foam looked like the perfect place to hammer out a home.
Within days NASA counted around 70 holes, some about 4 inches across, in insulation that shields super-cold fuel from the heat of launch.
Too many to patch on the pad. Discovery was rolled back to its hangar for repairs, and the launch slipped by more than a month.
NASA formed a Bird Investigation Review and Deterrent team: plastic owls, air horns, balloons painted with eyes. Discovery finally flew on July 13th.

description:
What if woodpeckers grounded a space shuttle? In June 1995 they did.
Northern flickers in nesting season pecked around 70 holes, some up to about 4 inches wide, into the foam insulation of Discovery's external fuel tank days before the STS-70 launch. The damage was too extensive to fix at the pad, so the shuttle was rolled back to the Vehicle Assembly Building and the launch slipped from 8 June to 13 July 1995. NASA set up a Bird Investigation Review and Deterrent (BIRD) team that used plastic owls, horns and balloons with painted eyes to keep the birds away.
